questions.subject: RESEARCH_METHODS
questions.topic: Coverage error created by a stale sampling frame
questions.learningObjective: Identify the bias from an outdated frame
questions.stem: An engineer's design brief lists a vendor address file last refreshed in 2019; what coverage problem does this stale frame create?

options.text: It has no effect on coverage because addresses are stable.
It guarantees every current unit still appears at least once.
options.misconception: assumes a frame never loses members over time

options.text: It omits units that moved or were created after 2019, producing undercoverage.
options.misconception: thinks stale frames only add duplicate listings

options.text: It only inflates variance without changing coverage.
options.misconception: confuses coverage error with sampling variance

questions.explanation: A stale frame can both omit new units and retain obsolete ones, but the item as worded treats stability as the tempting wrong idea. The correct reading is that coverage error arises from mismatches between frame and target population.
questions.hint: Ask whether the frame still matches the target population.

questions.subject: RESEARCH_METHODS
questions.topic: Inclusion probabilities assigned by a probability sample
questions.stem: Under simple random sampling without replacement, a population of 4000 units is sampled 200 units; what is each unit's inclusion probability?
questions.explanation: Inclusion probability equals n over N, so 200 divided by 4000 equals 0.05. The tempting error is to invert the ratio or treat it as a percentage without converting.
questions.hint: Divide sample size by population size.

options.text: Equal allocation across strata regardless of size or variance.
options.misconception: ignores stratum size and variance entirely

options.text: Neyman allocation proportional to stratum size times stratum standard deviation.
Proportional allocation by stratum size only.
options.misconception: omits the variance term in Neyman allocation

options.text: Allocate everything to the stratum with largest variance.
options.misconception: puts all sample in one stratum

questions.explanation: Neyman allocation weights each stratum by its size and standard deviation, reducing overall variance. Equal or purely proportional allocation misses the variance component.
